title: Model Cartography & Competitive Moat Scanner for Inference Routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
summary: Create an actionable competitive map and automated scanner that scores potential moat and routing-fit of open and hosted models for Redwood inference policies.
description: Goal: produce a repeatable product-oriented view (cartography) of competing models and an automated Moat Scanner that surfaces likely routing fallbacks, substitution risk, and economic impact for low-latency inference use-cases. Deliverables: 1) taxonomy of signals (latency, quant-compat, KV/seq support, license risk, throughput/cost profile), 2) interactive model cartography dashboard (fieldable by region and hardware tier), 3) Moat Scanner prototype that yields a ranked list of candidate fallback models and a substitution risk score for each customer archetype.
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy documented and reviewed by Research & Eng (latency, quantization compatibility, API deltas, licensing)
Dashboard prototype with filterable dimensions (region, hw class, sequence-length profile) deployed to internal console demo for SRE/SE review
Moat Scanner produces repeatable ranking for 3 canonical customer archetypes (chat-lowlatency, batch-embeddings, RAG-90pct) with reproducible scoring logic
Operational runbook documenting how scanner signals map to Redwood routing policies and suggested guardrails for automatic fallbacks
Stakeholder sign-off from GTM and SRE on customer-impact thresholds and alerting rules
